propositions: The query ticket digest is re-sent verbatim in the user message on every call in a batch, occupying the volatile block where it cannot be cached, despite being identical across all calls.
Hoisting the query digest into the system prompt makes the shared bytes sit in the cacheable prefix block, enabling one write plus N-1 cheap reads per review instead of N full-cost calls.

The measured cache floor for claude-sonnet-4-6 is 1024 tokens, not the 4096 documented for Opus; the hoisted prefix lands at 846 tokens, below the floor, so no cache benefit is realized on the measured corpus.

The relocation produces identical overlap-judge verdicts on 12 ordered pairs (6 candidates × 2 orderings) with no relation changes and no finding changes, preserving precision despite the prompt structure change.
The net token outcome is a +936 token regression (+5.8%) because the orientation paragraph reconciling the split prompt framing is carried on all calls without cache amortization.
